evals.prompt: I just recorded a clip from the loading dock camera and saved it at `/home/intel/videos/dock_cam_2026-07-15.mp4`. Can you upload it into VSS, tag it `dock,outdoor`, and make sure it's indexed so I can search it later?
evals.expected_output: Uploads `/home/intel/videos/dock_cam_2026-07-15.mp4` to VSS through `POST /manager/videos` as multipart field `video` with tags `dock,outdoor`, captures the returned `videoId`, triggers `POST /manager/videos/search-embeddings/<VIDEO_ID>`, re-checks the video record, and reports that the video is ready for later natural-language search.
expectations: Probes `GET /manager/health` and `GET /manager/app/features` before upload to confirm the backend is healthy and search is enabled.
Uses `POST /manager/videos` with multipart form field `video` and comma-separated `tags=dock,outdoor`.
Captures the returned `videoId` from the upload response.
Triggers embedding generation with `POST /manager/videos/search-embeddings/<VIDEO_ID>` because videos are not searchable until embeddings exist.
Re-checks `GET /manager/videos/<VIDEO_ID>` before telling the user the video is searchable.

evals.prompt: Search my video library for "person wearing a hat" and show me the top matching clips with their timestamps so I can jump straight to them.
evals.expected_output: Runs a one-off `POST /manager/search/query` for `person wearing a hat`, reads the wrapped response at `.results[].results[]`, and presents ranked clips with relevance score, segment start/end, seek timestamp, and video identifier or URL.
expectations: Probes manager health and search feature availability before querying.
Uses `POST /manager/search/query` with JSON containing the required `query` field set to `person wearing a hat`.
Parses the response as an object with ranked clips at `.results[].results[]`, not as a bare array.
Surfaces clip timing from `metadata.segment_start`, `metadata.segment_end`, and `metadata.seek_timestamp`.
Includes ranking information such as `metadata.relevance_score` and identifies the source with `metadata.video_id` or `metadata.video_url`.

evals.prompt: I need to find any forklift activity that happened indoors in the last 7 days. Search the videos tagged "indoor" for "forklift" and restrict it to that time window.
evals.expected_output: Runs `POST /manager/search/query` for `forklift` with `tags` set to `indoor` and a relative `timeFilter` of `{ "value": 7, "unit": "days" }`, then reports ranked clips with relevance scores, tags, clip windows, and seek timestamps.
expectations: Probes manager health and confirms search is enabled before querying.
Sends the required `query` value `forklift` to `POST /manager/search/query`.
Includes the optional comma-separated `tags` field with value `indoor`.
Uses a relative `timeFilter` with `value` 7 and `unit` `days`, one of the documented units.
Reads ranked clips from `.results[].results[]` and reports `relevance_score`, `segment_start`/`segment_end`, `seek_timestamp`, and `tags`.

evals.prompt: I uploaded a video yesterday but searches never return anything from it - I think the embedding job failed. Its video ID is `f079427b-5d3a-4e2b-9a11-6c0d8e2f9abc`. Can you check its status and regenerate the embeddings if needed?
evals.expected_output: Inspects `GET /manager/videos/f079427b-5d3a-4e2b-9a11-6c0d8e2f9abc`, retriggers embeddings with `POST /manager/videos/search-embeddings/f079427b-5d3a-4e2b-9a11-6c0d8e2f9abc` when embeddings are missing or failed, and re-checks the video record before reporting whether it can now be searched.
expectations: Checks manager health and search availability before the reindex workflow.
Inspects the existing video through `GET /manager/videos/<VIDEO_ID>` and treats the single record as wrapped under `.video`.
Uses `POST /manager/videos/search-embeddings/<VIDEO_ID>` to retry or regenerate embeddings.
Acknowledges that a video is not searchable until embeddings exist.
Re-checks the video record after triggering embeddings before declaring the retry complete.

evals.prompt: Run a search for "delivery truck backing up" across all my videos, but this time actually tell me the file names of the matching clips - not just some UUID. I need to know which recording to open.
evals.expected_output: Builds a video ID to filename map from `GET /manager/videos`, runs `POST /manager/search/query` for `delivery truck backing up`, joins each hit’s `metadata.video_id` to `.videos[].dataStore.fileName`, and presents ranked clips with filename, clip window, seek timestamp, and relevance score.
expectations: Uses `GET /manager/videos` and handles the response as an object containing `.videos`, not a bare array.
Builds the filename map from each video record’s `videoId` to `.dataStore.fileName`.
Runs the search with `POST /manager/search/query` and query text `delivery truck backing up`.
Reads hits from `.results[].results[]` and joins each `metadata.video_id` to the filename map because search results do not include filenames.
Presents top hits with filename plus `segment_start`/`segment_end`, `seek_timestamp`, and `relevance_score`.

evals.prompt: I want an ongoing alert for "worker without a safety vest" across the warehouse cameras - don't just run it once, save the query and turn on watching so it keeps re-checking as new video comes in. Also show me how to pull its latest results later.
evals.expected_output: Creates a stored search query for `worker without a safety vest` with `POST /manager/search`, enables watching with `PATCH /manager/search/<QUERY_ID>/watch` and `{ "watch": true }`, then explains how to fetch, refetch, list watched queries, and delete the query.
expectations: Probes manager health and search feature availability before creating the managed query.
Uses `POST /manager/search` with JSON containing `query: worker without a safety vest` to create a persistent query.
Captures the returned query identifier and enables watching with `PATCH /manager/search/<QUERY_ID>/watch` and `{"watch": true}`.
Explains checking latest results with `GET /manager/search/<QUERY_ID>` and manually rerunning with `POST /manager/search/<QUERY_ID>/refetch`.
Mentions listing watched queries with `GET /manager/search/watched` and cleanup with `DELETE /manager/search/<QUERY_ID>`.

evals.prompt: I just uploaded a new clip from the parking lot camera called `lot_cam_2026-07-20.mp4`. Please index it, then search my video library for "car alarm going off" and give me the ranked clips with timestamps.
evals.expected_output: Before indexing the clip or running the search, the skill unconditionally runs scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh to resolve the VSS app root by checking the enclosing git repo's remote for the official VSS project or a fork of it, reusing that checkout if found or otherwise doing a shallow single-branch sparse checkout of sample-applications/video-search-and-summarization from main, then cd's into the resolved app root before uploading/indexing the video and running the search query.
expectations: The answer runs the bundled bootstrap helper (scripts/vss-bootstrap.sh) as an unconditional first step, before uploading/indexing the video or running the search, even though the prompt never asked about setup, location, or cloning.

The bootstrap check determines whether the current location is already a valid clone/checkout (or a fork) of the VSS project by inspecting the enclosing git repository's remote configuration (e.g. `git remote -v`, origin/upstream URL) to see if it points at open-edge-platform/edge-ai-libraries or a fork of it, not merely by checking for local marker files.
If that check finds a valid existing checkout (the user's own clone or a fork whose remote traces back to the official repo), the answer states it is reused and states that NO re-clone is performed.
If no valid checkout/remote is found, the answer performs a shallow, single-branch, sparse checkout of only sample-applications/video-search-and-summarization from main.
The answer changes directory (cd "$APP_ROOT") into the resolved app root before running any of the skill's real commands for the upload/index/search task.
